description:
Scope / functional specification: Planning only for lib/zaq/engine/messages/conversation_identity.ex missed line 38 (1-based). The module's @moduledoc says Channels derives transport-neutral identity; Engine and Agent consume JSON-safe identifiers. Line 38 is the public channel_config_id/1 catch-all for non-map identity, returning nil. Coverage-only tests; do not edit production, support modules, existing tests, documentation or Git state. Exclusive test path to ADD: test/zaq/engine/messages/conversation_identity_test.exs. This is a single independent test surface and issue, with no new dependencies.

Tests to add before implementation (implementation here means tests only):
1. Primary missed-line example: alias Zaq.Engine.Messages.ConversationIdentity; use ExUnit.Case, async: true. Assert ConversationIdentity.channel_config_id(nil) == nil. Also assert ConversationIdentity.channel_config_id("123") == nil (a string is not a map, even if numeric). Optionally test [] to establish non-map/list rejection; avoid exhaustive unrelated types merely for line coverage. These calls select the catch-all at line 38, not the map case's wildcard at line 34. An absent or malformed identity must not acquire a channel configuration ID.
2. Nearby guard controls in the SAME new file, so the miss cannot be 'fixed' by an incorrect always-nil function: assert channel_config_id(%{"channel_config_id" => 7}) == 7; assert channel_config_id(%{"channel_config_id" => 0}) == nil; assert channel_config_id(%{"channel_config_id" => "7"}) == nil; assert channel_config_id(%{}) == nil. The contract accepts positive INTEGER values from stamped JSON-safe identity only, not parseable strings; don't conflate this function with Incoming's other coordinate normalizer. Exact values differentiate the valid map arm (line 33), invalid map arm (line 34), and non-map arm (line 38). No database or Channels adapter needed.
3. Optional related public-API examples if whole-module coverage is requested after measurement: identifier(%{"key" => "  room  "}, "key") == "room"; identifier(%{"key" => 42}, "key") == "42"; identifier(%{"key" => "   "}, "key") == nil; normalize(nil) == nil. Do not call identifier/2 on non-map/non-binary-key inputs: it has no fallback clause, and that failure is not line 38's contract. Existing test/zaq/engine/messages/incoming_identifier_property_test.exs already establishes numeric/string coordinate equivalence for Incoming; don't modify or duplicate its property.

Branches and assertions: primary nil and numeric-looking binary inputs must return exact nil through line 38; companion valid and invalid map values prove fail-closed strict typing while retaining positive ID. No permission grants or identity attestation is implied by this pure normalizer. Assert return values only, not private calls or instrumentation. No fixtures, helper extraction, Mox, external network, Repo/SQL Sandbox, application-env mutation, process names, sleeps, timing waits or event synchronization. Keep async: true. Source callers include Conversations' identity projection (identifier for key/channel/participant/thread and channel_config_id for config); no integration fixture is needed to reach this pure public guard. No E2E: no user journey or behavior change.

Property assessment: this single missed catch-all is a finite guard boundary, so concrete examples are more diagnostic than a new property. IncomingIdentifierPropertyTest already exercises the broad numeric/string normalization invariant in its own caller; if scope later expands to arbitrary input safety, consider a bounded ExUnitProperties property that non-map inputs never produce an ID, alongside the explicit nil regression. Avoid generated structs/maps that accidentally satisfy is_map/1 and enter the other clause.

Action reuse assessment: not applicable — only tests for existing ConversationIdentity.channel_config_id/1; no executable operation, Action, tool, workflow Step, caller or dispatch boundary is being added, altered or orchestrated. Production owning module stays unchanged. Documentation updates: none for test-only coverage; record validation and exceptions in this issue / eventual PR.

Validation handoff for later implementer, NOT performed in this planning task: write the primary failing/missed-line test first and companion controls; run isolated mix test test/zaq/engine/messages/conversation_identity_test.exs and mix q via Context Mode, keep logs out of context, inspect test-only diff. At post-review coverage phase generate fresh mix coveralls.json (600000 ms) then, only if successful, mix coverup and confirm source line 38 executed; do not trust a stale report. Follow workflow final mix precommit (900000 ms) before requesting final human approval. Never weaken existing assertions. Unreachable blockers: none identified: non-map arguments match the public fallback directly. If fresh coverage disagrees, check source revision/instrumentation and actual call shape before claiming success; document any verified blocker, do not add test-only production seams. No tests, coverage or Git changes were run by this planner.
